title: Fail-close error written via ctx.session.state is invisible to the pipeline node's ctx.state readers (terminal envelope + final-gate guard) under the production state split the fix itself documents
evidence: agent.py:632 `finalize_boundary_gate(ctx.session.state)`; boundary_compliance_remediation.py:356 `state[STATE_PIPELINE_ERROR] = {` (state == the live session dict); agent.py:797 `yield _content_event(ctx, build_response_envelope(ctx.state))`; envelope.py:64 `pipeline_error = state.get(STATE_PIPELINE_ERROR)`; agent.py:658 `if ctx.state.get(STATE_PIPELINE_ERROR):`; the fix's own model comment at agent.py:596-597: "absent from this node's ctx.state snapshot taken at construction"
detail: Under the fix's own divergence model, finalize's error write to the live dict is invisible to ctx.state readers — the envelope degrades to retryable ANALYSIS_FAILED (the #156 retry storm) and first-error-wins misses sibling errors.
recommended_fix: Mirror the error into ctx.state after finalize (or pass both views into finalize) so agent.py:658 and build_response_envelope(ctx.state) still see the non-retryable COMPLIANCE_VIOLATION; keep first-error-wins reading the wrapper.

title: Unsolicited rename compliance.review_unparseable -> compliance.review_unparsable breaks an existing unit test and a stable telemetry event-name contract
evidence: compliance_enforcement.py:239 `"compliance.review_unparsable",` (diff: `-"compliance.review_unparseable",` / `+"compliance.review_unparsable",`); test_verification_compliance_judge.py:491 `r for r in caplog.records if r.message == "compliance.review_unparseable"`; verified by running: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_verification_compliance_judge.py::test_unparseable_review_emits_failed_rollup` -> FAILED (ValueError); full unit run: 1 failed, 2041 passed
detail: Not in the spec; breaks test_unparseable_review_emits_failed_rollup (verified red at the reviewed sha — the PR's '2042 unit tests pass' claim is false); event names are a stable BigQuery/Sentry observable contract, so the rename silently orphans external queries.
recommended_fix: Revert the rename to compliance.review_unparseable (or, if intentional, update the test AND disclose the contract change in the PR with a BQ/Sentry migration note); the suite must be green at the reviewed sha.

title: Verdict-stamp write side (judge callback -> state) has no test coverage; the new regression tests seed the stamp manually
evidence: compliance_enforcement.py:132 `def _stamp_review_verdict(` (invoked from _emit_review_telemetry / _emit_failed_review_rollup); test_gate_state_marshalling.py:164 `STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT: {"judge_kind": "boundary", "passed": True}` (seeded, not produced); grep of test_verification_compliance_judge.py / test_final_compliance_reviewer.py: zero references to STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT
detail: The independent-witness chain (criterion 4) is verified by code-reading only: no test asserts the judge callbacks write the stamp. A regression in the stamp wiring would go undetected by the suite.
recommended_fix: Add assertions to the callback unit tests that log_boundary_compliance_review / log_final_compliance_review leave STATE_COMPLIANCE_REVIEW_VERDICT with the judge's passed/attempt values.
